findings.title: Legacy SQL command construction bypasses the new disabled check
findings.body: UnmarshalSQLCommand still constructs a SQLCommand via NewSQLCommand without checking whether SQL expressions are disabled; only ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery in reader.go has the new gate. This legacy entry point is therefore protected only indirectly because the stub DB makes sql.TablesList fail, returning a misleading BadRequest 'error reading SQL command' instead of an explicit disabled/not-implemented rejection. If the DuckDB-backed DB implementation is restored or replaced, this path will silently re-enable the CVE-2024-9264 surface without passing through the reader check. Gate both construction paths (or remove/stub UnmarshalSQLCommand/NewSQLCommand) so disabling does not depend on a downstream stub error.

findings.title: enableSqlExpressions is dead, inverted logic that always returns false
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions computes enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions), then returns false in the if branch and false unconditionally afterwards, so the feature-flag check has no effect and the function name/contract is misleading. The current behavior (always disabled) matches the PR intent, but a future maintainer trying to re-enable SQL expressions behind the flag will find flipping the toggle does nothing and may 'fix' the wrong branch, accidentally re-enabling it insecurely. Make the disable explicit (e.g. return false with a comment referencing the CVE/removal, or delete the helper and inline the rejection) instead of leaving inverted dead logic.

findings.title: No regression test that SQL expressions are rejected even with the feature flag on
findings.body: This is a security fix for CVE-2024-9264 (RCE/LFI via DuckDB SQL expressions), but the PR adds no test asserting that a QueryTypeSQL expression is rejected when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled, nor that the legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand path cannot execute SQL. Without such a test, restoring the go-duck dependency or simplifying enableSqlExpressions back to a plain flag check would reintroduce the vulnerability with no failing test. Add tests covering both entry points with the flag on and off.

findings.title: go.work.sum churn is inconsistent with the go.mod/go.sum dependency removal
findings.body: go.mod/go.sum drop go-duck and its transitive deps (apache/thrift, klauspost/asmfmt, minio/asm2plan9s, minio/c2goasm, JohnCGriffin/overflow), yet go.work.sum re-adds hashes for several of those same modules while dropping unrelated ones (Azure azblob, google go-replayers). This suggests the workspace sums were not regenerated with go work sync after the removal and may fail verification or resurrect the removed DuckDB transitive graph for other workspace modules. Regenerate and verify go.work.sum so the vulnerable dependency is actually gone from the whole workspace, not just the main module.
